rules.deny: Monitor is disabled. Use Bash with run_in_background to spawn a blocking waiter that exits on the next event.
Monitor call has no command string that the Bash guard rules can check; refusing it rather than running it unchecked.
Malformed bash command ({{ errors[0] }}). Fix the syntax and retry.
find rooted at / is disabled. Scan a specific directory instead.
find must specify -xdev so it does not cross filesystem boundaries. To search several filesystems, issue a separate find -xdev per filesystem.
pgrep -f and pkill -f can match helper processes spawned by the harness (e.g. its bash -c wrapper), and pkill would kill them. Use pgrep -af, confirm each match cmdline, then kill by PID.
Do not capture pgrep output in a pipe or substitution ($(...), `...`, <(...)). Let pgrep print straight to stdout and read the result.

An "until grep ..." (or "while ! grep ...") loop never exits if the process writing the log silently dies. Watch the process instead: tail -f --pid=<PID> <log> | grep -m1 <pattern> (tail stops when the process exits, ending the pipeline either way). Run it with run_in_background.

sudo is disabled: passwordless sudo is insecure, and a password prompt needs a TTY, which Bash processes spawned by Claude Code do not have. Use run0 instead, which shows the user a graphical auth prompt every time and does not cache authentication.
